chunks: And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil ibn Darraj, from some of our companions, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them) that he said:
"When the wife who has not been consummated is divorced, she becomes permanently divorced by a single pronouncement."
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on divorce before consummation in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib* clarifies that for a wife not yet consummated with, a single pronouncement of divorce is irrevocable (*banan*), distinguishing it from the revocable phase (*raj'i*) after consummation. This ruling is significant in Shia jurisprudence as it simplifies the waiting period (*iddah*) to two menstrual cycles rather than three, reflecting the reduced financial obligations and lack of full marital rights prior to intimacy.
